name: papers-graph
description: Reality check: facts and glossary terms extracted from four arXiv papers (Transformer 1706.03762, ReAct 2210.03629, LoRA 2106.09685, RAG 2005.11401). Facts form a graph across papers (e.g. LoRA adapts Transformer attention weights; ReAct acts on Wikipedia like RAG's index; RAG retrieves into BART, a Transformer descendant). Levels: L0 = direct lookup, L1 = one hop, L2 = two hops, L3 = multi-hop/cross-paper synthesis.

source_papers.transformer: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
source_papers.react: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (Yao et al., 2022)
source_papers.lora: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models (Hu et al., 2021)
source_papers.rag: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (Lewis et al., 2020)

facts: The Transformer model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task
The Transformer was proposed by Vaswani et al. at Google in 2017
cases.question: What BLEU score does the Transformer achieve on WMT 2014 English-to-German translation?
cases.expected_answer: 28.4 BLEU

facts: ReAct was published at ICLR 2023 by Yao et al. from Princeton and Google Brain
ReAct interleaves reasoning traces with task-specific actions in LLMs
cases.question: At which venue was ReAct published?
cases.expected_answer: ICLR 2023

facts: RAG combines a parametric memory (a pre-trained seq2seq model) with a non-parametric memory (a dense vector index of Wikipedia)
The retriever in RAG is DPR, the Dense Passage Retriever
cases.question: What are the two types of memory combined in a RAG model?
cases.expected_answer: Parametric memory (pre-trained seq2seq model) and non-parametric memory (dense vector index of Wikipedia).

facts: LoRA freezes pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture
LoRA checkpoints reduced size roughly 10,000x, from 350GB to 35MB on GPT-3 175B
cases.question: What does LoRA do with the pre-trained model weights during adaptation?
cases.expected_answer: It freezes them and injects trainable low-rank decomposition matrices instead.

facts: ReAct overcomes hallucination in chain-of-thought reasoning by interacting with a simple Wikipedia API
ReAct outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning methods by absolute success rates of 34% on ALFWorld and 10% on WebShop
cases.question: Which external tool does ReAct interact with for question answering?
cases.expected_answer: A simple Wikipedia API.

facts: The Transformer establishes a single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 on WMT 2014 English-to-French after training 3.5 days on eight GPUs
The big Transformer models were trained for 300,000 steps (3.5 days) at about 1.0 second per step
cases.question: How many GPUs were used to train the model that scored 41.8 BLEU?
reasoning_chain: 41.8 BLEU fact mentions 'trained 3.5 days on eight GPUs'
cases.expected_answer: Eight NVIDIA P100 GPUs.

facts: LoRA adapts only attention weight matrices (Wq, Wv) and freezes MLP modules for parameter efficiency
Adapting only query and value projection matrices reduced checkpoint size roughly 10,000x, from 350GB to 35MB
cases.question: Which weight matrices does LoRA adapt to achieve the 10,000x checkpoint reduction?
reasoning_chain: 10,000x reduction fact
that fact is about 'query and value projection matrices'
cases.expected_answer: The query and value projection matrices (Wq, Wv) of the attention layers.

facts: In RAG, the seq2seq generator is BART and the retriever is DPR (Dense Passage Retriever)
DPR provides latent documents conditioned on the input, which BART conditions on to generate output
cases.question: Which model generates the final output in RAG, and what does it condition on besides the input?
reasoning_chain: generator is BART
BART conditions on latent documents from DPR
cases.expected_answer: BART generates the output, conditioned on the input plus latent documents retrieved by DPR.

facts: ReAct outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning methods on ALFWorld and WebShop
On ALFWorld ReAct improves absolute success rate by 34%, using only one or two in-context examples
cases.question: How many in-context examples does ReAct need to beat RL baselines on ALFWorld?
reasoning_chain: ALFWorld +34%
same sentence: 'while being prompted with only one or two in-context examples'
cases.expected_answer: Only one or two in-context examples.

facts: The Transformer improves over existing best results including ensembles by over 2 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German
The Transformer achieves 28.4 BLEU on that task
cases.question: What was the approximate BLEU score of the previous best results on WMT 2014 English-to-German that the Transformer surpassed?
reasoning_chain: Transformer scores 28.4
improvement is 'over 2 BLEU'
=> prior best ~26.x
cases.expected_answer: Around 26 BLEU (28.4 minus the stated improvement of over 2 BLEU).

facts: LoRA injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture
A very low rank (r = 1 or 2) suffices for LoRA even when the full rank d is as high as 12,288 on GPT-3 175B
GPT-3 175B full fine-tuning deployment is prohibitively expensive because each fine-tuned instance has 175B parameters
cases.question: Why is LoRA especially valuable for deploying many task-specific variants of GPT-3 175B?
reasoning_chain: deploying each full fine-tuned instance = 175B params, prohibitive
LoRA freezes base weights
only tiny rank-r matrices trained/swapped
=> swap small adapters per task at tiny cost
cases.expected_answer: Because full fine-tuned instances each carry 175B parameters — prohibitively expensive to deploy per task. LoRA freezes the base model and trains only tiny rank-r matrices (r=1–2 suffice vs d=12,288), so switching tasks means swapping megabytes of adapter weights, not 350GB checkpoints.

facts: RAG's non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia
ReAct overcomes chain-of-thought hallucination by interacting with a Wikipedia API
ReAct generates human-like task-solving trajectories more interpretable than baselines without reasoning traces
cases.question: Both RAG and ReAct ground LLMs in Wikipedia, but how do their mechanisms differ?
reasoning_chain: RAG: differentiable retrieval via dense vector index feeding generation
ReAct: discrete API actions interleaved with reasoning traces
=> parametric-retrieval vs agentic-action grounding
cases.expected_answer: RAG grounds via a differentiable dense vector index of Wikipedia integrated end-to-end into generation; ReAct grounds via discrete Wikipedia API actions interleaved with explicit reasoning traces, prioritizing interpretability and fact verification.

facts: The Transformer removes recurrence entirely and relies solely on attention mechanisms
Training the big Transformer took 3.5 days on 8 GPUs for 300,000 steps
The best previous models were recurrent/convolutional encoder-decoder architectures with much higher training costs
cases.question: Why could the Transformer be trained in a small fraction of the training costs of prior state-of-the-art models?
reasoning_chain: prior SOTA = recurrent/convolutional
Transformer removes recurrence, all-attention
attention parallelizes across sequence
=> far less sequential compute => 3.5 days vs literature
cases.expected_answer: Prior models were recurrent/convolutional — inherently sequential. The Transformer removes recurrence in favor of attention, which parallelizes across the sequence during training, cutting training to 3.5 days on 8 GPUs.

facts: LoRA limits its study to adapting attention weights in the Transformer and freezes the MLP modules
The Transformer's attention uses scaled dot-product queries, keys and values produced by projection matrices Wq, Wk, Wv
Rank r = 4 or 8 with {Wq, Wv} performs on par with or better than full fine-tuning on WikiSQL and MultiNLI
cases.question: Why does adapting only Wq and Wv make sense given how the Transformer computes attention?
reasoning_chain: attention = softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V
Q,K,V come from Wq,Wk,Wv projections
LoRA shows Wq,Wv alone matches full adaptation at low rank
=> attention content is where task adaptation lives; MLP frozen for efficiency
cases.expected_answer: Attention itself is computed from Q/K/V projections (Wq, Wk, Wv); LoRA's ablations show adapting just Wq and Wv at ranks as low as 4–8 matches full fine-tuning on WikiSQL/MultiNLI, so capturing task-specific behavior in the attention projections while freezing MLPs captures most adaptation value at minimal cost.

facts: ReAct was evaluated on HotpotQA (QA), Fever (fact verification), ALFWorld and WebShop (interactive decision making)
ReAct overcomes hallucination and error propagation issues prevalent in chain-of-thought reasoning
Chain-of-thought prompting is reasoning without interaction with external environments
cases.question: What problem does ReAct share with plain chain-of-thought, and what does it add to fix it?
reasoning_chain: CoT = internal reasoning only
CoT suffers hallucination + error propagation
ReAct keeps reasoning traces but adds environment actions (Wikipedia API etc.)
=> actions ground reasoning in external evidence
cases.expected_answer: Both generate reasoning traces, but plain CoT hallucinates and propagates errors internally. ReAct keeps the traces and interleaves real environment actions (Wikipedia API, ALFWorld/WebShop), letting it consult external evidence instead of inventing it.

facts: LoRA injects trainable matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture
The Transformer's self-attention lets every token attend to every other token, removing recurrence
LoRA checkpoint sizes shrink ~10,000x because only attention projections are adapted at low rank
RAG marginalizes latent documents with a top-K approximation
cases.question: If you wanted to build a LoRA-adapted, RAG-augmented assistant today, why do all four papers matter to its design, and which architectural inheritance connects them?
reasoning_chain: assistant backbone = Transformer family
LoRA adapts that backbone cheaply (its target architecture IS the Transformer)
RAG adds non-parametric knowledge via retrieval into a seq2seq (BART = Transformer descendant)
ReAct-style action loop would let the assistant decide when to retrieve
=> common ancestor: Transformer attention; papers compose as backbone + cheap adaptation + retrieval grounding + agentic control
cases.expected_answer: All four compose into one system: the Transformer is the backbone architecture everything inherits from; LoRA makes adapting that backbone per-task cheap (10,000x smaller checkpoints); RAG supplies fresh non-parametric knowledge by retrieving into an index rather than relying on frozen parameters; and ReAct provides the control loop deciding when to reason versus act/retrieve. The connecting thread is Transformer attention — every paper either builds it, adapts it efficiently, wraps retrieval around it, or orchestrates it with actions.
required_memories: ReAct OR reasoning traces OR actions

facts: RAG addresses provenance and world-knowledge-update problems left open by parametric-only LLMs
LoRA enables swapping task adaptations by exchanging small adapter weights instead of full model copies
The Transformer achieves strong generalization across tasks like translation and constituency parsing
ReAct trajectories are more human-interpretable and trustworthy than baselines
cases.question: Trace how the four papers collectively address four production concerns: knowledge freshness, provenance, serving cost, and debuggability.
reasoning_chain: knowledge freshness: parametric LLMs can't update easily -> RAG's non-parametric index updates independently
provenance: RAG cites retrieved documents; ReAct exposes explicit action traces
serving cost: LoRA swaps MB-scale adapters not GB-scale models
debuggability: ReAct's interpretable trajectories + RAG's retrievable evidence vs opaque parametric recall
cases.expected_answer: Knowledge freshness: RAG's non-parametric Wikipedia index updates without retraining. Provenance: RAG can cite what it retrieved; ReAct logs explicit reasoning/action traces showing why each step happened. Serving cost: LoRA serves one frozen base plus swappable megabyte adapters instead of one deployed model per task. Debuggability: ReAct's human-readable trajectories and RAG's retrievable evidence replace opaque parametric recall with inspectable decisions.
required_memories: provenance OR provenance for their decisions

facts: The Transformer achieved 28.4 BLEU (En-De) and 41.8 BLEU (En-Fr), new state-of-the-art at publication
ReAct improves success rates on ALFWorld (+34%) and WebShop (+10%) over imitation/RL
LoRA matches GPT-3 175B full fine-tuning performance on WikiSQL and MultiNLI with r=4 or 8 on {Wq, Wv}
RAG achieves state-of-the-art results on open-domain QA benchmarks
cases.question: Across all four papers, compare what 'improvement' means: which claim is hardest to verify independently and why?
reasoning_chain: BLEU/success-rate/accuracy claims = benchmark numbers, reproducible with public datasets/code
LoRA's parity claim requires replicating GPT-3-scale runs — closed model, huge compute
=> LoRA's claim hardest: depends on proprietary 175B model access
cases.expected_answer: The Transformer's BLEU scores, ReAct's success rates, and RAG's QA numbers are all verifiable against public benchmarks and released code/data. LoRA's central claim — matching full GPT-3 175B fine-tuning — is hardest to verify independently, because it depends on reproducing experiments with a proprietary 175-billion-parameter model and substantial compute that few groups have.

facts: RAG's parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq model; BART is that seq2seq model
BART is a Transformer-based denoising autoencoder
LoRA injects trainable matrices into Transformer layers
The Transformer relies wholly on self-attention without recurrence
cases.question: Could LoRA be applied directly inside RAG? Walk the dependency chain through the papers.
reasoning_chain: RAG's generator = BART
BART is a Transformer variant
LoRA targets Transformer layer projections
=> yes: apply LoRA to BART's attention weights, keeping the frozen base and swapping task adapters while DPR index stays independent
caveat: RAG trains end-to-end through retrieval; freezing most weights changes that dynamic
cases.expected_answer: Yes. The chain: RAG's parametric memory is BART; BART is a Transformer-family encoder-decoder; LoRA injects trainable low-rank matrices specifically into Transformer attention projections. So one could freeze BART inside RAG and attach LoRA adapters for domain specialization. The caveat: RAG was trained end-to-end, backpropagating through retrieval — with LoRA only adapter weights train, so the retriever-generator co-adaptation dynamics would change and likely need separate tuning of DPR.

facts: The Transformer paper introduced scaled dot-product attention and multi-head attention
Multi-head attention projects into subspaces with learned linear projections (Wq, Wk, Wv, Wo)
LoRA adapts attention projection matrices at low rank
ReAct and RAG both consume Transformer-descendant models
Scaling laws imply larger models benefit most from parameter-efficient adaptation
cases.question: Construct the causal chain from 'scaled dot-product attention' to 'why agent frameworks today use LoRA': connect every paper in order.
reasoning_chain: multi-head attention needs learned Wq/Wk/Wv/Wo projections
those projections dominate parameter count scaling with model size d
full fine-tuning of them becomes infeasible at GPT-3 scale -> LoRA low-rank adaptation of exactly those matrices
adapted Transformers power RAG generators and ReAct policy LLMs
-> agents use LoRA to get specialized behavior per task/domain cheaply
cases.expected_answer: Multi-head attention requires learned projection matrices (Wq, Wk, Wv, Wo) whose parameter counts grow with model dimensionality. As models scaled toward GPT-3 175B, fully retraining those projections per task became infeasible — LoRA exploits exactly this structure by injecting low-rank updates into those same attention projections. The resulting cheaply-adapted Transformer descendants are what RAG uses as generators and ReAct steers as reasoning-and-acting policies. Hence modern agent frameworks standardize on LoRA: they need many specialized behaviors over one shared Transformer backbone, and attention-projection adapters deliver that at swap-in-seconds cost.
